text:
sarah: Heads up: noticed 8-12% P99 token latency bump on nightly after driver 12.11.1 + Triton 2.5. We hit it on long-tail small-batch workloads. CI perf alert triggered.
mike: which tests? long-seq or smallbatch?
sarah: smallbatch (1-4 tokens), kv-heavy chat workload. perf job: runtimes/nightly/rt-smallbatch-p99. got numbers: before 12.11.1: 27ms P99, after: 31ms P99
alex: :eyes: can you paste the perf log?
sarah: ```
# rt-smallbatch-p99
before: p50=8.2ms p95=14.5ms p99=27.1ms
after:  p50=8.5ms p95=15.3ms p99=31.0ms
autotune.log: selector chose gemm_tile32_v2 for many kernels (previously tile64)
nvlink: observed higher cudaLaunchKernel count and longer kernel enqueue latency
```
jen: I saw a ton of kernel flips in the autotune logs, plus increased kernel-launch overhead. Looks like Triton changed heuristic for tile size.
perf-bot: CI PERF WARNING: rt-smallbatch-p99 increased by 14% (231s -> 264s) on merge 0b3a9f2 triggered at 2365432050
mike: Bisect candidates: driver bump, triton upgrade, and a CUDA patch. Any recent merges touching selector heuristics?
sarah: There was a runtime change to prefetch eviction order last week but that was canaryed. I'll run a quick bisect between triton revs and driver.
alex: Running A/B locally: pinned driver 12.10 vs 12.11.1, Triton 2.4 vs 2.5. Repro: driver+triton combo causes kernel selection flip to smaller GEMM path, + extra global sync.
jen: Can you paste nvprof output?
alex: ```
== nvprof summary ==
Kernel: gemm_tile64_v1   calls=1024  total_time=1.8s  avg=1.76ms
Kernel: gemm_tile32_v2   calls=1400  total_time=2.6s  avg=1.86ms  # more launches, worse occupancy
cudaLaunchKernel count: +18%
memcpy HtoD stalls: +10%
SM utilization: -7%
notes: autotune table picked tile32 path on seq<=8 workloads after Triton update
```
sarah: I'm going to rollback Triton in nightly and re-run CI. Also opening a triton-issue.
release-bot: Created issue in triton: https://github.com/triton-inference-server/issues/482 kernel-autotune-heuristic-change-impacts-small-batch-latency
mike: If triton fix isn't fast we should put a temporary autotune override: force preferred kernel for small sequences. Can you add a heuristic gate?
jen: I can cook a patch that pins selector for seq<=8 to tile64 path. Will send PR.
sarah: Thanks. For tracking: root cause seems to be combined change in triton autotune table + driver scheduling that alters preferred kernel ordering; KV prefetch eviction amplified it because smaller kernel causes higher launch rate.
alex: Note: perf impact on production would be worse for a mix of small and tiny requests. Watch rollout.
mike: :thumbsup: schedule revert if CI doesn't pass after revert.
